title: Testing Cytological Adequacy and Insertion Depth for Anal Self-Sampling: A Pilot Intervention Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Anal cancer screening consensus guidelines were released in 2024. Although anal cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) tests are currently performed in a clinic by a healthcare provider, there is increasing interest in providing individuals with the option to collect a sample themselves. Our objective was to compare the performance characteristics and acceptability of a swab inserted at two different depths for anal cytology self-sampling. METHODS: We recruited sexual and gender minority individuals to complete anal cytology self-sampling and a survey. Participants were randomized to either a 3- or 5-cm insertion depth, then given a demonstration and a kit to complete onsite in a private bathroom. Cytopathology and reflex HPV testing were conducted. RESULTS: Fifty individuals completed anal cytology self-sampling and a post-swab survey, with 23 participants randomized to the 5-cm insertion depth and 27 participants randomized to the 3-cm depth. Although not significant, the proportion of cytologically adequate specimens was higher with a 5-cm insertion (87.0%, 95% CI 66.4%-97.2%) compared to a 3-cm insertion (70.4%, 95% CI 49.8%-86.2%). A higher proportion of specimens collected squamocolumnar junction cells with the 5-cm insertion depth (47.8%, 95% CI 26.8%-69.4%) compared to the 3-cm insertion (29.6%, 95% CI 13.8%-50.2%) though this difference was non-significant. Acceptability was high and not associated with insertion depth. CONCLUSIONS: Swabs inserted 5 cm for anal cytology self-sampling collected a non-significantly higher proportion of cytologically adequate and squamocolumnar junction cells compared to 3 cm, with no difference in acceptability. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07085845.

title: Exosomes as Molecular Mediators of Reproductive Health: From Infertility to HPV-Related Disease
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the biological roles of exosomes in reproductive physiology, examines their involvement in mechanisms associated with female and male infertility, and discusses their emerging role in human papillomavirus (HPV)-related reproductive disease. Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by transporting proteins, lipids, DNA, messenger RNAs (mRNAs), microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and other bioactive molecules, thereby regulating the biological functions of recipient cells. Particular emphasis is placed on the roles of exosomes in folliculogenesis, gametogenesis, fertilization, embryo implantation, and spermatogenesis. Alterations in exosomal cargo and function have been reported in several female and male reproductive disorders. In parallel, emerging evidence suggests that exosomes may participate in HPV-associated disease through mechanisms involving viral persistence, modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, and transfer of viral and host-derived molecules between cells. Exosomes are also being investigated as potential non-invasive biomarkers and therapeutic delivery platforms; however, these applications remain largely investigational. Importantly, substantial heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation, purification, and characterization methods limits cross-study comparability and remains a major barrier to clinical translation. Overall, current evidence supports exosome-mediated communication as a biologically relevant mechanism across reproductive physiology, infertility-related disorders, and HPV-associated disease, while further standardized and clinically validated studies are required to establish their diagnostic and therapeutic utility.

Alterations in exosomal cargo and function have been reported in several female and male reproductive disorders. In parallel, emerging evidence suggests that exosomes may participate in HPV-associated disease through mechanisms involving viral persistence, modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, and transfer of viral and host-derived molecules between cells. Exosomes are also being investigated as potential non-invasive biomarkers and therapeutic delivery platforms; however, these applications remain largely investigational. Importantly, substantial heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation, purification, and characterization methods limits cross-study comparability and remains a major barrier to clinical translation. Overall, current evidence supports exosome-mediated communication as a biologically relevant mechanism across reproductive physiology, infertility-related disorders, and HPV-associated disease, while further standardized and clinically validated studies are required to establish their diagnostic and therapeutic utility.

title: Current status and future perspectives of treatment de-escalation in localized head and neck cancer.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) often requires invasive multimodal therapy, including surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Although these interventions have improved treatment outcomes, patients frequently experience long-term functional impairment and treatment-related morbidity. Consequently, clinical research has shifted toward treatment de-escalation, a paradigm aimed at preserving quality of life while maintaining oncologic control. This review summarizes the current evidence from prospective clinical trials on de-escalation strategies for HNSCC of the oropharynx, hypopharynx, larynx, and oral cavity, with a focus on radiotherapy-based approaches. Investigators have evaluated several de-escalation strategies, including total radiation dose reduction in definitive chemoradiotherapy, modification or omission of concurrent systemic therapy, de-intensification of prophylactic nodal irradiation, response-adapted treatment de-intensification, and minimally invasive approaches such as transoral surgery with risk-adapted postoperative therapy. These strategies target favorable-risk populations, particularly patients with human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal cancer. Although numerous phase II studies have reported encouraging clinical outcomes and acceptable toxicity profiles, definitive evidence supporting the safety and efficacy of de-escalation strategies remains unestablished in large-scale phase III trials. Unwarranted de-escalation for HNSCC should be avoided, particularly for medically fit patients, and promising strategies require validation in phase III trials before routine clinical adoption. Future challenges include prospective validation through clinical trials and the integration of predictive biomarkers to balance the delicate trade-off between toxicity reduction and oncologic safety.

title: Vaccine attitudes and perceptions in a post-COVID Era: what lessons can be learned in Tunisia?
abstract: Abstract Introduction Although the COVID-19 pandemic clearly showed the potential consequences of a world without vaccinations, vaccine hesitancy is likely to be more pronounced in the post-COVID-19 era. The introduction of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in this context is likely to raise particular concerns. In Tunisia, decision-makers have prioritized the introduction of HPV vaccine into the immunization schedule. This study assessed individual barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccine acceptability in Tunisia, with the aim of guiding an effective communication strategy for HPV vaccination campaigns in Tunisia and neighboring countries in a post-pandemic context. Methods Using a qualitative design, we conducted 14 focus groups (FG) with healthcare professionals (HCP) (N=32) and community representatives (CR) (N=89) in five regions of the country. The discussion followed a semi-structured guide designed on the basis of vaccine hesitancy determinants matrix. Transcripts were deductively analyzed according to the “social processes” and “thinking and feeling” of the behavioural and social drivers (BeSD) Framework. Inductive approach was used to analyze participants’ suggestions for promoting HPV vaccination. Results The FG analysis demonstrated that the historically strong trust in vaccination in Tunisia has weakened after the COVID-19 pandemic. Mistrust of health system and experts, the pandemic management and vaccine mandates measures had negative influence on the vaccine attitudes in a post pandemic Tunisian context. Persistent concerns about COVID-19 vaccines safety were frequently intertwined with widespread distrust of pharmaceutical companies and their profit motives, perceived as imposing inequitable access and lower-quality vaccines on countries in the Global South. These concerns fueled confusion about vaccine’s side effects. The weakening of immunity was recurring, as well as memory issues, impacts on fertility, and sudden deaths. Regarding information, our research revealed that although digital platforms were perceived as widely used, a significant part of the population interviewed considered public TV channel, as the most reliable source of health information. Conclusions Emphasizing how the pandemic has shaped individual and collective perceptions and attitudes toward vaccination, our findings underline the importance of leveraging lessons learned from the pandemic to develop a context tailored and coherent communication strategy for successful HPV vaccine implementation.

title: HPV vaccine coverage among adults aged 27–45: Implications for oropharyngeal cancer prevention
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection contributes to rising incidence of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancer (OPC). expanded HPV vaccination to adults aged 27-45 y in 2018, COVID-19 caused preventive visits and routine immunizations to plunge. We analyzed 2019 and 2022 NHIS data among adults aged 27-45 (2019 n = 8,745; 2022 n = 7,303). The primary outcome was ever HPV vaccination (≥1 dose), regardless of age at first vaccination. We estimated age-adjusted, survey-weighted coverage and used multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds of vaccination by sociodemographic characteristics; secondary 2022 analyses assessed initiation between ages 27 and 45. Ever HPV vaccine uptake increased from 15.1% in 2019 to 20.7% in 2022 (difference 5.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.03-7.07). In both years, lower odds were observed with increasing age, men, non-Hispanic Asian adults, individuals with lower educational attainment, and those without a usual place for care. By 2022, lower income-to-poverty ratios and lack of insurance were associated with reduced odds, whereas LGB+ and unmarried adults had higher odds, and adults in the Northeast had higher odds than those in the South. Only 1.43% (95% CI, 1.07-1.80) initiated vaccination between ages 27 and 45 in 2022. Initiation was more common among females, LGB+ and non-Hispanic Asian adults, and unmarried adults, and less common among those with lower education and no usual place for care. The increase in lifetime HPV vaccine coverage likely reflects childhood and adolescent vaccination rather than initiation at ages 27-45, which remained uncommon, and persistent inequities highlight missed opportunities for equitable OPC prevention.

The study analyzed NHIS data from 2019 and 2022, finding that ever HPV vaccine uptake increased from 15.1% to 20.7% during this period. title: Update in the Molecular Pathogenesis of Sebaceous Carcinoma
abstract: Sebaceous carcinoma is an uncommon but potentially aggressive adnexal malignancy whose molecular pathogenesis has been substantially clarified in recent years. Rather than representing a single molecular entity, sebaceous carcinoma is now understood as a biologically heterogeneous group of tumors arising through distinct yet sometimes overlapping oncogenic pathways. Recent genomic and multi-omics studies have identified several major molecular subsets, including mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR)/microsatellite instability (MSI)-associated tumors, ultraviolet (UV) radiation-driven tumors, and pauci-mutational tumors characterized predominantly by alterations in cell-cycle and epithelial differentiation regulators such as TP53, RB1, and ZNF750. These findings have also reinforced biologically relevant differences between ocular and extraocular sebaceous carcinoma, with periocular tumors more often enriched for TP53/RB1/ZNF750-driven mechanisms and extraocular tumors more frequently showing UV-related and dMMR signatures. In addition to these core pathways, recent evidence has highlighted the contribution of NOTCH signaling, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway alterations, copy-number changes including MYC amplification, rare human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cases, and emerging transcriptomic abnormalities involving cholesterol metabolism and sebaceous differentiation programs. These advances not only deepen current understanding of sebaceous carcinoma biology but also have important diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications, particularly in relation to Lynch/Muir–Torre syndrome screening, molecular subclassification, and the potential use of immune checkpoint inhibitors and other targeted strategies in selected patients. This review provides an updated overview of the molecular pathogenesis of sebaceous carcinoma, focusing on the main genomic, transcriptomic, and biologically actionable alterations described to date, and discusses their implications for tumor classification, pathogenesis, and future translational research.

title: Sexual behavior-related exposures, sexually transmitted infections, and viral markers in relation to prostate cancer risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Sexual behavior, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and viral markers have been investigated in relation to prostate cancer, but heterogeneous exposure definitions and ascertainment methods complicate interpretation. We synthesized observational evidence separately across biologically and methodologically distinct exposure domains. Methods We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase.com , and Web of Science Core Collection from inception through 27 May 2026. Eligible studies were comparative observational studies evaluating sexual behavior-related exposures, STI history or serology, or viral markers in relation to prostate cancer. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for sufficiently comparable estimates. Risk of bias was assessed using Newcastle-Ottawa Scale domains, supplemented by design-specific epidemiological considerations. GRADE was used as a post-registration evidence-certainty assessment. Results Of 121 reports assessed for eligibility, 57 primary observational reports were included after final eligibility reconciliation. Twenty-five reports entered at least one pooled model and three additional reports appeared only in descriptive forest plots. For tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection, the observed pooled association was OR 3.01 (95% CI 1.97-4.61; I2=36.2%; prediction interval 1.15-7.91; 13 studies). HPV16 and HPV18 tissue/PCR subtype estimates were also elevated, whereas HPV serology showed no clear association. Estimates for Trichomonas vaginalis serology and history-based STI exposure were imprecise or heterogeneous, and sexual-behavior exposures were too heterogeneous for pooling. Certainty was very low across all evaluated exposure domains. Conclusions Tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection was more frequent among prostate cancer cases in the available comparative studies, but the evidence is very uncertain because of risk of bias, limited temporal clarity, sampling and comparator differences, and other methodological limitations. These findings should not be interpreted as establishing an etiologic or causal effect and do not support prostate-cancer prevention recommendations based on HPV vaccination, STI screening, or sexual-behavior modification. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1334823 , identified: CRD420261334823.

title: A new microsimulation model of HPV natural history for comparison of novel cervical screening strategies
abstract: Abstract Background The cost-effectiveness of cervical cancer screening strategies is estimated by health decision models. Fidelity to HPV natural history and multi-state carcinogenesis is critical to improve evaluations of new screening tests. Methods We developed a new health decision model of the HPV genotype-specific causal pathway to cervical cancer based on cohort, trial, and cross-sectional data. The novel model presents several new approaches in representing early HPV natural history: 1) transitions between health states are estimated by new statistical approaches adapted to handle intermittently-observed data; 2) transitions are directly estimated from observational data (i.e., statistically identifiable) rather than calibrated to fit; and 3) precancer is rigorously defined using histopathology and HPV genotyping as a surrogate for cancer risk. Results We present a model for pending policy decisions in Brazil. Model outputs closely match age-specific prevalence data from São Paulo for thirteen carcinogenic HPV types 16/18/31/33/35/45/52/58 (modeled individually) and 39/51/56/59/68 (grouped). The model-projected median age of precancer is 30.0 years (95% CI: 27.9—32.3 years). Conclusions By restricting model health states and transitions to the essential, directly observable causal pathway, our approach can generate metrics with measurable standard errors for cost-effectiveness analyses. Comparative modeling analyses are underway to assess differences in results relative to existing state-of-the-art models. Our approach can be generalized to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of an HPV-based screen-triage-treat approach with extended genotyping that has been demonstrated efficacious in nine PAVE Consortium countries.

title: Comparison of intradermal purified protein derivative (PPD) and vitamin D3 in the treatment of non-genital cutaneous warts.
abstract: Background Viral warts are a common skin infection, usually on the hands, feet, or face of children and young adults, and are caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV) due to lower immune resistance. The common types seen in Pakistan are common warts, plantar warts, and flat warts, which cause pain or cosmetic concern among patients. Aims To compare and evaluate the efficacy of intralesional purified protein derivative (PPD) and vitamin D3 in the management of viral non-genital cutaneous warts. Methods A retrospective, comparative study was conducted at Nishtar Medical University Hospital, Multan, Pakistan from January to July 2023. A total of 266 patients with 1–10 viral warts were divided into two groups: Group I was given intralesional PPD (0.1 mL of 10 TU), and Group II was given intralesional vitamin D3 (0.5 mL of 600,000 IU), each given at 2-week intervals for a maximum of four doses. Summary The mean age of participants was 42.84 ± 13.29 years, with a male predominance (67.3%). Complete clearance of warts was significantly higher in the PPD group (85.7%) compared to the vitamin D3 group (71.4%; P = .005). Subgroup analysis revealed better outcomes with PPD in younger patients with multiple warts and specific anatomical locations (palmar, plantar, trunk), while vitamin D3 showed superior clearance for limb warts. Intralesional PPD demonstrated superior efficacy compared to vitamin D3 in the treatment of viral warts. Both therapies were safe and well-tolerated. This study provides direct comparative evidence of distinct immunological mechanisms, offering practical insights for the management of recalcitrant warts.

title: Oncobiome relation with HPV and Gynecological cancer
abstract: By now, it is well understood that the human body is inhabited by millions of tiny organisms that are alive and found in different parts of our body that called microbiota. Over the past decades, these tiny microorganisms have worked together like a smart network that links to human health, and any alterations or dysbiosis in this network lead to different disorders as well as cancer development. Hence, many preclinical and clinical studies have focused on clarifying the exact role of microflora in cancer development. One of these cancers is gynecological cancer, which is considered a major threat to health in the female population. In the case of gynecological malignancy, the presence and persistent infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is also important. Persistent infection with HPV leads to alterations in the commensal population of microbiota in the vagina and even the gut, resulting in cancer progression. Therefore, we aimed to comprehensively review the current knowledge on the interaction between gut microbiota and vaginal microbiota in HPV acquisition, favoring gynecological cancer development.

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 有证据表明,HPV 感染引起的微生物群变化可能导致癌症进展,但这些相互作用的确切机制和程度仍不清楚。需要进行更详细的研究来阐明特定微生物群变化在不同 HPV 相关癌症中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,需要进一步研究来探索肠道和阴道微生物群与 HPV 感染之间的具体相互作用。这可能会导致更好的预防 HPV 相关癌症的策略,诊断 和 治疗。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the interaction between gut microbiota and vaginal microbiota in HPV acquisition and its role in favoring gynecological cancer development. The central question is to comprehensively understand how these microbiota interactions influence HPV-related diseases.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of preclinical and clinical studies that explore the relationship between microbiota and HPV. It does not explicitly report on the databases used, search dates, or eligibility criteria, but it includes a range of studies examining the microbiota's role in cancer progression.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that persistent HPV infection leads to alterations in the vaginal and gut microbiota, which may contribute to cancer progression. It highlights the importance of understanding these interactions in the context of HPV-associated diseases.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence suggests that alterations in microbiota due to HPV infection may lead to cancer progression, but the exact mechanisms and the extent of these interactions remain unclear. There is a need for more detailed studies to clarify the role of specific microbiota changes in different HPV-related cancers.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies that further research is needed to explore the specific interactions between gut and vaginal microbiota and HPV infection. This could lead to better strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of HPV-associated cancers.

title_zh: 肿瘤生物组与 HPV 和妇科癌症的关系
source_body_en: By now, it is well understood that the human body is inhabited by millions of tiny organisms that are alive and found in different parts of our body that called microbiota. Over the past decades, these tiny microorganisms have worked together like a smart network that links to human health, and any alterations or dysbiosis in this network lead to different disorders as well as cancer development. Hence, many preclinical and clinical studies have focused on clarifying the exact role of microflora in cancer development. One of these cancers is gynecological cancer, which is considered a major threat to health in the female population. In the case of gynecological malignancy, the presence and persistent infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is also important. Persistent infection with HPV leads to alterations in the commensal population of microbiota in the vagina and even the gut, resulting in cancer progression. Therefore, we aimed to comprehensively review the current knowledge on the interaction between gut microbiota and vaginal microbiota in HPV acquisition, favoring gynecological cancer development.

title: DIAGNOSTIC EFFECTIVENESS OF SELF-SAMPLING FOR HPV TESTING AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION MODEL IN KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: Relevance: The effectiveness of cervical cancer prevention is still limited by incomplete screening coverage among socially vulnerable groups and women who have not previously participated in the survey. Self-collection of a vaginal sample for human papillomavirus (HPV) testing reduces barriers associated with clinical sampling, but its effectiveness depends on the validity of the test system and the triage of positive results. The study aimed to summarize current data on diagnostic effectiveness, the introduction of HPV self-sampling, and to propose a model for Kazakhstan. Materials and Methods: This structured narrative review included publications, regulatory sources, and literature lists from January 2021 to July 2026 and indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE. Results: When using clinically validated PCR tests, the total sensitivity of CIN2+ detection is 89.7% for self-taken vaginal samples and 92.9% for samples taken by a healthcare professional. Direct mailing provides the greatest increase in participation, and a closed loop of support is necessary to prevent losses after a positive test. Conclusion: Self-sampling should be implemented as an additional organized route with registration, selection of a validated devicetest pair, information, and guaranteed triage. A step-by-step model is optimal for Kazakhstan, focusing primarily on the underserved, overstayed, and rural women.
journal: Eurasian Journal of Oncology and Radiology

source_records.title: DIAGNOSTIC EFFECTIVENESS OF SELF-SAMPLING FOR HPV TESTING AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION MODEL IN KAZAKHSTAN
source_records.abstract: Relevance: The effectiveness of cervical cancer prevention is still limited by incomplete screening coverage among socially vulnerable groups and women who have not previously participated in the survey. Self-collection of a vaginal sample for human papillomavirus (HPV) testing reduces barriers associated with clinical sampling, but its effectiveness depends on the validity of the test system and the triage of positive results. The study aimed to summarize current data on diagnostic effectiveness, the introduction of HPV self-sampling, and to propose a model for Kazakhstan. Materials and Methods: This structured narrative review included publications, regulatory sources, and literature lists from January 2021 to July 2026 and indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE. Results: When using clinically validated PCR tests, the total sensitivity of CIN2+ detection is 89.7% for self-taken vaginal samples and 92.9% for samples taken by a healthcare professional. Direct mailing provides the greatest increase in participation, and a closed loop of support is necessary to prevent losses after a positive test. Conclusion: Self-sampling should be implemented as an additional organized route with registration, selection of a validated devicetest pair, information, and guaranteed triage. A step-by-step model is optimal for Kazakhstan, focusing primarily on the underserved, overstayed, and rural women.

title: Assessing HPV Vaccination Prevalence, Knowledge and Attitudes among Clinical Medical and Dental Students In KNUST, Ghana
abstract: Background: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of cervical cancer, which remains a major public health concern in Ghana. Although HPV vaccination is a proven preventive measure, uptake in low- and middle-income countries remains low. As future healthcare providers, medical and dental students are key advocates for vaccination, yet their own knowledge and vaccination practices are not well understood. This study assessed the prevalence of HPV vaccination, knowledge, attitudes and observed the association between socioeconomic status and vaccine uptake among clinical medical and dental students at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).

title: Rates of HPV Vaccination among Women and People with a Cervix Living with HIV in Canada.
abstract: HPV vaccination is the primary method of preventing cervical cancer. Due to the high prevalence of HPV infection in women with HIV, we sought to determine the rates of HPV vaccination among women with HIV in Canada. The NOVA-HIV study assessing HPV vaccine dosing is currently recruiting women with HIV. As part of the screening protocol, the vaccination status of patients was evaluated to determine eligibility for study recruitment. Of the 505 women with HIV who have been screened across five study sites, 47.2% were vaccinated. More efforts are needed to increase HPV vaccine access and uptake among this population.

title: Clinical spectrum of penile intraepithelial neoplasia in a sexual health service: a retrospective case series.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) is an uncommon precursor to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Its heterogeneous appearance may overlap with inflammatory penile dermatoses, genital warts, or infection, potentially delaying diagnosis. We aimed to characterise the clinical spectrum, inflammatory context, biopsy triggers, histopathology, management, and outcomes of histopathologically confirmed PeIN presenting to a sexual health service. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of patients with histopathologically confirmed low-grade or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, or invasive SCC, assessed at Melbourne Sexual Health Centre, Australia, from 2018-2025. Electronic records were reviewed for demographics, immune status, circumcision status, lesion site and morphology, symptoms, coexisting inflammatory disease, biopsy indications, histopathology, treatment, recurrence, and follow-up. Data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Thirteen patients aged 25-72 years were identified; four had lichen sclerosus and three had immunosuppression or immune-modifying therapy. Most were uncircumcised at diagnosis. Lesions predominantly involved the glans or inner foreskin, but also occurred on the shaft, and showed marked heterogeneity, including erythematous or white plaques, papules, warty or hyperkeratotic lesions, erosions, fissures, and ulcerated nodules. Symptoms ranged from none to pain, burning, itch, hypersensitivity, malodour, and non-healing sores. Several lesions initially appeared inflammatory or wart-like; sometimes in the setting of documented lichen sclerosus. Biopsy was generally prompted by persistence, focal hyperkeratosis or induration, ulceration or erosion, architectural change, progressive enlargement, or incomplete response to empiric therapy. Histopathology showed predominantly high-grade lesions; one patient had low-grade disease with biopsy-confirmed recurrence, and two had invasive SCC. All cases were HPV-associated by reported histopathological features and/or p16 positivity. Management was frequently multimodal and multidisciplinary, including circumcision, local or wide excision, partial penectomy, imiquimod, 5-fluorouracil, cryotherapy, and treatment of coexisting inflammation. Outcomes were generally favourable where documented, although recurrence or suspected recurrence occurred in some patients and ongoing surveillance was often required. CONCLUSIONS: PeIN presenting to sexual health services is clinically diverse and commonly embedded within an inflammatory clinical narrative. Persistent or atypical penile lesions, particularly those showing focal change or incomplete treatment response, warrant a low threshold for biopsy and coordinated dermatology-urology management.

title: Retrospective study of inflammatory markers in high-grade cervical lesions.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation markers for abnormal cervical screening results and high-grade cervical lesions in women participating in a human papillomavirus- and cytology-based screening program, thereby determining colposcopy indications more accurately to reduce unnecessary colposcopy requests and prevent overtreatment. METHODS: A total of 2,758 women who underwent cervical cancer screening between 2020 and 2025 were included in this retrospective cross-sectional study. Abnormal screening results were defined as abnormal cytology (≥Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance [ASC-US]) and/or high-risk human papillomavirus positivity. Hematological parameters measured within 1 month prior to screening were used to calculate neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index. Continuous variables were evaluated using nonparametric tests, and the independent predictors of abnormal screening results and high-grade lesions were identified using logistic regression models. RESULTS: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index values were significantly higher in the abnormal smear groups and in human papillomavirus -positive patients (all p 4.41, sensitivity 66.7%, specificity 99.2%), followed by systemic immune-inflammation index (area under the curve=0.847), while platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio showed lower specificity (area under the curve=0.741). CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our findings suggest that inflammatory markers are associated with abnormal cervical screening results. To determine the significance and clinical utility of serum inflammatory markers, multicenter clinical trials involving larger patient cohorts are needed.

title: Assessing knowledge, attitudes and practices towards HPV vaccination among male healthcare professionals and students in Delhi National Capital Region: a mixed-method study
abstract: Abstract Introduction Cervical cancer poses a significant health risk to women globally and in India. While the burden of HPV (Human papillomavirus)-related infections among Indian women is well-documented, there is a need to understand HPV related dynamics among Indian men as well as an influencing factor in male reproductive health. This study aims to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to HPV vaccination among male healthcare professionals in the Delhi National Capital Region (NCR), India. Methods A mixed-method survey was conducted from March 2022 to April 2023 among young male healthcare professionals from diverse backgrounds across public and private healthcare settings in the Delhi NCR of India. In the quantitative arm, convenience sampling was employed to recruit participants, with 299 complete responses recorded. For the qualitative arm, 37 participants were interviewed to gain an in-depth understanding of their perceptions of HPV infection and vaccination. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics (SPSS Version 30.0), and qualitative data analysis was done using the manual transcription method employing the Grounded Theory Approach (GTA). Results The mean age of the participants in the quantitative arm was 24.6 years. The overall knowledge score towards HPV vaccination was 59%, while the attitude score was 89%. Although 83.9% of participants were willing to promote HPV vaccination among men in India, only 11.4% got vaccinated for HPV. The engagement in unsafe sexual practices was significantly associated with age ( p = 0.006), occupation ( p = 0.004), education ( p < 0.001), and marital status of the participants ( p = 0.003). A significant association was also observed between marital status and the willingness to engage in HPV-related awareness within their personal networks ( p< 0.001). In the qualitative arm, the mean age was 32.4 ± 6.2 years. Four themes were generated after thematic analysis:1) HPV seen as female-specific, 2) Awareness not translating into action, 3) Systemic silence and missed opportunities, and 4) Cost-consciousness despite awareness. Out of 37 interviewees, 27% had misconceptions about HPV, 18.9% felt a lack of a male-focused HPV vaccination drive, and 29.7% expressed affordability concerns about getting an HPV vaccination due to the high vaccine cost. Conclusion This study's findings lay the groundwork for more extensive research to understand the barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination among male healthcare professionals. Comprehensive educational, institutional, and policy interventions are required to improve vaccine uptake and support equitable implementation of gender-neutral HPV vaccination.

title: Transoral Robotic Surgery in the Treatment of Head and Neck Cancer: Application and Prospect
abstract: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) has reshaped the surgical management of head and neck neoplasms since its introduction in the mid-2000s, offering a minimally invasive transoral route to lesions of the oropharynx, larynx, hypopharynx, and nasopharynx. This narrative review synthesizes the technical foundations, current clinical evidence, and emerging directions of TORS, with explicit attention to study rigor and evidentiary hierarchy. Powered by the da Vinci platform, TORS provides magnified three-dimensional visualization and wristed instrumentation that enable en bloc resection with reduced external morbidity, shorter hospitalization, and the potential to spare or de-intensify adjuvant radiotherapy in selected human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal cancers. For early-stage oropharyngeal disease, local control rates of 90–95% and disease-specific survival above 90% are consistently reported, and recent systematic reviews and large multicenter cohorts, including the international Recurrent Tumors of the Upper Aerodigestive Tract (RECUT) experience, confirm durable oncologic and functional outcomes in both primary and salvage settings, although randomized trials have yielded nuanced, sometimes divergent quality-of-life results. We appraise outcomes by anatomical subsite, the de-escalation trial landscape, complications and their mitigation, learning-curve dynamics, health economics, and the rapidly evolving integration of artificial intelligence in segmentation, augmented-reality navigation, intraoperative margin assessment, and outcome prediction. Recent evidence confirms that TORS is a valuable but expertise-dependent option whose benefit is greatest in carefully selected patients managed within multidisciplinary, high-volume pathways. We conclude by defining the principal unresolved questions and the evidence required to position TORS appropriately within contemporary multidisciplinary care.

title: Toll-like receptor expression across histological states of Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis
abstract: Abstract Epidermodysplasia verruciformis (EV) is characterized by susceptibility to cutaneous β-human papillomaviruses, persistent viral lesions and an increased risk of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). We investigated whether expression of Toll-like receptors 3, 4, 5 and 9 (TLR3, TLR4, TLR5 and TLR9) differs across histological states within EV. Immunoreactivity was quantified by digital H-score using QuPath in 97 specimens from 28 patients, comprising 13 lesion-free skin samples, 15 flat warts and 69 cSCCs. Prespecified comparisons evaluated flat wart versus lesion-free skin, cSCC versus non-neoplastic tissue and invasive versus in situ cSCC, with invasive tumour differentiation assessed secondarily. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equations and false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction were used for inference. After correction for multiple testing, TLR9 H-scores were higher in flat warts than in lesion-free skin (β=60.58; q=0.0332). Compared with non-neoplastic tissue, cSCC showed lower TLR3 (β=−81.40; q=0.00745), higher TLR4 (β=55.59; q=0.04793) and lower TLR9 expression (β=−34.80; q=0.03412). TLR5 showed a nominal increase in cSCC that did not meet the FDR threshold. None of the four receptors differed significantly between invasive and in situ cSCC, and no differentiation trend remained significant after FDR correction. These findings show receptor-specific differences in TLR expression across histological states of EV, particularly involving TLR3, TLR4 and TLR9, although the diagnostic and prognostic significance of these tissue patterns remains to be established.

title: TỶ LỆ NHIỄM VÀ ĐẶC ĐIỂM PHÂN BỐ KIỂU GEN HPV NGUY CƠ CAO Ở PHỤ NỮ LÀM XÉT NGHIỆM TẠI BỆNH VIỆN ĐA KHOA TÂM ANH NĂM 2025
abstract: Đặt vấn đề: Ung thư cổ tử cung liên quan chặt chẽ đến nhiễm Human Papillomavirus (HPV), đặc biệt là các genotype nguy cơ cao (HR-HPV). Phân bố genotype thay đổi theo khu vực, đặc điểm dân số và hệ thống sàng lọc; dữ liệu tại các bệnh viện tư nhân lớn ở Việt Nam còn hạn chế. Mục tiêu: Xác định tỷ lệ nhiễm HR-HPV, mô tả phân bố genotype theo nhóm tuổi và tình trạng đồng nhiễm ở phụ nữ làm xét nghiệm tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tâm Anh. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang hồi cứu trên 6.606 mẫu phết cổ tử cung từ ngày 01/01/2025 đến 31/12/2025. Xét nghiệm real-time PCR được thực hiện trên Cobas 5800 và Alinity m. Tỷ lệ được trình bày với khoảng tin cậy 95% (95% CI); khác biệt giữa các nhóm tuổi được đánh giá bằng kiểm định Chi-square. Kết quả: Có 928/6.606 mẫu dương tính HR-HPV, tương ứng 14,05% (95% CI: 13,23–14,91). HPV16, HPV18 và Other HR-HPV được phát hiện lần lượt ở 2,44%, 1,39% và 11,43% tổng số mẫu. Tỷ lệ nhiễm cao nhất ở nhóm <30 tuổi (16,87%), tiếp theo là nhóm ≥50 tuổi (15,83%); khác biệt giữa các nhóm tuổi có ý nghĩa thống kê (χ2 = 17,24; df = 3; p < 0,001). Đồng nhiễm từ hai nhóm genotype trở lên chiếm 8,08% số trường hợp dương tính. Kết luận: Tỷ lệ nhiễm HR-HPV là 14,05%; Other HR-HPV chiếm ưu thế và tỷ lệ nhiễm cao hơn ở phụ nữ <30 tuổi và ≥50 tuổi.

title: Efficacy and safety of CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy for cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions in women of childbearing age: a retrospective single-arm study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy in reproductive-age women with cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL). METHODS: This retrospective single-arm study included 57 reproductive-age women with biopsy-proven cervical HSIL and high-risk HPV infection who received CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-ALA-PDT between January 2022 and June 2025. RESULTS: At 6 months, the overall response to the initial combined treatment was 92.98% (53/57), with cure in 84.21% (48/57), improvement in 8.77% (5/57), and persistent HSIL in 7.02% (4/57). The four patients with persistent HSIL received rescue LEEP. At 12 months, when the four rescue LEEP patients were counted as treatment failures for the initial combined regimen, cure was 84.21% (48/57) and overall response was 92.98% (53/57). After including rescue LEEP as a separate rescue-treatment outcome, all 57 patients had normal TCT and normal histopathology; 52/57 (91.23%) were cured and 5/57 (8.77%) had persistent HR-HPV and were classified as improved. Thus, the 100% (57/57) 12-month overall response includes four patients who achieved normal histology after rescue LEEP and cannot be attributed to CO2 laser ablation plus 5-ALA-PDT alone. HPV clearance for the initial combined treatment was 48/57 (84.21%) at 6 months and 48/57 (84.21%) at 12 months when the four rescue LEEP patients were counted as initial treatment failures; the final 12-month HPV clearance rate including rescue LEEP was 52/57 (91.23%). CONCLUSION: CO2 laser ablation followed by 5-ALA-PDT is associated with high histological remission and HR-HPV clearance and a mild adverse-event profile in selected reproductive-age women with cervical HSIL. However, the 100% 12-month overall response includes four patients who received rescue LEEP and cannot be attributed to CO2 laser ablation plus 5-ALA-PDT alone. This single-arm study cannot establish the incremental benefit of laser ablation over PDT alone or of PDT over laser ablation. Cervical adhesions occurred in 7.02% (4/57), and cervical length, cervical function, fertility, and obstetric outcomes were not assessed; anatomical preservation cannot be equated with functional or fertility protection.

title: Mandates without backlash: COVID-19 vaccine policies and the uptake of other vaccines
abstract: Abstract This paper examines whether mandatory COVID-19 vaccination policies generated spillover effects on the uptake of other vaccines. Using a global country-year panel, we combine COVID-19 vaccine mandate data from the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker with international vaccination coverage data for discretionary vaccines, including Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and Influenza, and routine childhood vaccines, including Measles-containing, Rubella-containing, Diphtheria-Tetanus-Pertussis (DTP)-containing, Polio-containing, Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)-containing, Hepatitis B-containing, Rotavirus-containing, and Pneumococcal-containing vaccines. The treatment is measured by a binary indicator that equals 1 if a country adopted any COVID-19 vaccine mandate. To address staggered mandate adoption and treatment effect heterogeneity across countries, we estimate dynamic average treatment effects for switching countries using the de Chaisemartin and D’Haultfoeuille (2026) staggered difference-in-differences estimator. Overall, we find no systematic evidence of declines in national coverage rates for other vaccines following COVID-19 vaccine mandate adoption. This is true for almost all vaccines studied. However, for some routine childhood vaccines, evidence of differential pre-treatment trends warrants caution in interpreting those estimates as definitive evidence of no causal effect. Power and sensitivity analyses show that, for seven routine outcomes, first-period declines can be excluded under moderate departures from parallel trends.

title: Beyond the Oropharynx: TTMV-HPV DNA Detection in a p16-Positive Hypopharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Plasma TTMV-HPV16 DNA provided complementary molecular evidence in a p16-positive hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, while PET/CT localized the occult left pyriform sinus primary. Serial postoperative TTMV-HPV DNA assays remained undetectable through approximately 19 months of clinical and radiographic surveillance.

title: Cost-effectiveness of self-sampling strategies for cervical cancer screening: a commentary.
abstract: Tackling cervical cancer represents a global health priority and relies on preventative approaches such as screening. To increase uptake, self-sampling strategies used to detect human papillomaviruses have shown promise of cost-effectiveness. This commentary critically appraises an economic evaluation comparing first-void urine and vaginal swab self-sampling strategies against clinician-collected cervical samples in the UK. While the self-sampling strategies could improve screening uptake among non-attenders and health outcomes, the impacts on the subsequent incidence of cervical cancer and types of cancer stage for non-attenders should have been considered. Higher screening uptake, while increasing early detection, would also imply an increase in the number of diagnostic and follow-up appointments, for example for cytology and colposcopies. Future research should bridge these gaps as well as investigating the differential effects on socio-economic sub-groups and the views of eligible women to facilitate a wider implementation of self-sampling strategies.

title: Associated factors and control measures for cervical precancerous lesions in the Mifi Health District, Cameroon: a case-control study
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in low- and middle-income countries, despite being largely preventable. In Cameroon’s Mifi Health District, preventive services remain underused. We identified factors associated with cervical precancerous lesions and assessed selected control measures. A retrospective case-control study was conducted at Bafoussam Regional Hospital in 2024 among 348 women aged 30-49: 87 cases (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions [LSIL] or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions [HSIL]) and 261 controls with normal cytology (1:3 ratio). Logistic regression was used; control measures were compared with World Health Organization (WHO) elimination targets. Lesions were independently associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) 16/18 positivity (adjusted odds ratio [ORa]=5.94; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-9.5), non-use of condoms (ORa=4.2; 95% CI: 2.1-8.5), gynecological symptoms (ORa=3.7; 95% CI: 2.0-6.8), HIV seropositivity (ORa=3.6), hormonal contraception ≥5 years (ORa=3.5), history of sexually transmitted infections (STIs; ORa=2.3), low education (ORa=2.1) and smoking (ORa=1.8). HPV vaccination coverage was 7%, screening coverage 0.43%, and 60% of screen-positive women were treated (performance score: 3/10). Multiple risk factors and major prevention gaps were identified. Strengthening HPV vaccination, screening and timely treatment is essential.

title: Le programme de dépistage du cancer du col de l’utérus en Algérie par le frottis cervico-utérin est-il efficace ?
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer is a major public health issue in Algeria, where a national screening program based on the Pap smear was launched in 2001. However, its effectiveness has never been rigorously evaluated. This study aimed to assess the impact of the screening program on cervical cancer incidence in the province of Oran between 1996 and 2020. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Oran Cancer Registry and included all cervical cancer cases diagnosed between 1996 and 2020. Age-standardized incidence rates based on the world standard population were calculated, and an age-period-cohort modeling approach was applied to examine trends according to age, diagnostic period, and birth cohort. RESULTS: Over the study period, 1,872 cases of cervical cancer were recorded. The age-standardized incidence rate decreased from 25.8 to 8.8 per 100,000 women between 1996 and 2020. However, a significant rebound in relative risk was observed beginning in 2011, with a peak during the 2016–2020 period. Cohort analysis showed a lower risk among more recent generations, while the highest incidence was observed among women aged 50–59. CONCLUSION: Although the overall incidence of cervical cancer declined over the study period, the recent resurgence calls into question the effectiveness of the screening program. An integrated strategy—including human papillomavirus vaccination, organized screening, and health education—is essential to achieve World Health Organization targets.

title: Cognitive and behavioral determinants of HPV vaccination willingness and Behavior among female university students in Karnataka, India
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination remains a critical public health strategy for preventing HPV-related diseases; however, vaccination uptake continues to be influenced by multiple psychological and contextual factors. This study examines the determinants of willingness to vaccinate (WTV) and vaccination behavior (VB) by integrating constructs from the Health Belief Model, Protection Motivation Theory, and the 3Cs framework, including perceived severity (PS), perceived vulnerability (PV), complacency (COM), and vaccine confidence (CONF). A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data on individuals' perceptions, attitudes, willingness to vaccinate, and vaccination behavior. The study tested the direct effects of PS, PV, COM, and CONF on WTV, the mediating role of WTV in predicting VB, and the moderating effects of HPV vaccine recommendations and HPV-related information sources on the proposed relationships. The findings demonstrate that perceived severity, perceived vulnerability, and vaccine confidence positively influence willingness to vaccinate, whereas complacency negatively affects willingness. WTV significantly mediates the relationships between PS, PV, COM, CONF, and vaccination behavior. Moderation analysis revealed limited but significant moderating effects: HPV vaccine recommendations and HPV-related information sources strengthened selected relationships within the model, while several proposed moderation effects were not statistically supported. This study provides an integrated framework for understanding HPV vaccination behavior by combining cognitive, motivational, and contextual determinants. The findings highlight the importance of enhancing risk awareness, reducing complacency, strengthening vaccine confidence, and leveraging effective recommendations and information channels to improve HPV vaccine uptake. These insights offer practical implications for designing targeted public health communication and vaccination promotion strategies.

title: Primary Cervical Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma Incidentally Diagnosed During Evaluation of High-Grade Cervical Dysplasia: A Case Report
abstract: Primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the uterine cervix is a rare extranodal malignancy that may mimic more common cervical pathologies.We report the case of a 33-year-old woman with human papillomavirus (HPV)-16 positivity who was found to have cervical DLBCL incidentally during evaluation and treatment of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).Histopathologic analysis following repeat excisional procedure revealed DLBCL, germinal center B-cell subtype, without residual epithelial dysplasia.Staging positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake confined to the cervix and central uterine cavity, without nodal or distant involvement.Bone marrow and endometrial biopsies were negative.The disease was classified as stage IE extranodal DLBCL with low-risk features.The patient was treated with four cycles of R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) using a PET-adapted approach based on the Intergroup S1001 trial and achieved a complete metabolic response.This case highlights an uncommon presentation of cervical lymphoma, the importance of accurate histopathologic diagnosis, and the role of PET-adapted therapy in limited-stage disease.

title: Case Report: Successful treatment of verruciform acanthotic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia with 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy
abstract: Verruciform acanthotic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (vaVIN) is a rare, human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent, p53 wild-type intraepithelial precursor of the vulva, and standardized therapies for this disease are currently lacking. We report the case of a 68-year-old woman who presented with a 2-year history of multiple warty papules and vulvar pruritus and was diagnosed with vaVIN on the basis of histopathology (verruciform acanthosis with compact orthokeratosis, hypogranulosis, and superficial keratinocyte pallor with minimal cytologic atypia) and immunohistochemistry (HPV negativity, a p53 wild-type pattern, and non-block p16 expression) analyses. She underwent 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) and achieved complete clinical remission, with no recurrence during the follow-up period. To our knowledge, reports on the use of photodynamic therapy for vaVIN are scarce. This case suggests that ALA-PDT may be a promising alternative treatment option for vaVIN.

title: Interpretable machine learning prioritizes transcriptomic features associated with ferroptosis-mitochondrial permeability transition net activity states in cervical cancer
abstract: Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical carcinogenesis involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and altered non-apoptotic cell-death programs. Ferroptosis and mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT)-driven necrosis may share upstream stress-related transcriptional signals, but their joint pathway-state features in cervical cancer remain incompletely characterized. Methods We constructed a directionality-aware net pathway activity framework using evidence-audited ferroptosis-promoting, ferroptosis-inhibitory, MPT-promoting, and MPT-inhibitory gene sets in 304 TCGA-CESC primary tumors. The score was benchmarked against ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE and evaluated in controlled simulations. For feature prioritization, score-defining genes were excluded from predictors and Elastic Net feature selection, XGBoost tuning, and model fitting were performed strictly within repeated nested cross-validation. Outer-test SHAP, model-sensitivity analysis, and a 200-permutation complete-pipeline test were used for interpretation and robustness assessment. External validation used GSE138080, GSE63514, GSE223804, and GSE151666. Results CombinedNet showed moderate-to-high concordance with ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE (Spearman rho = 0.735, 0.882, and 0.943, respectively), while 1,300 controlled simulations showed strong recovery of the latent promoter-minus-inhibitor balance across scenarios and effect sizes (mean rho = 0.944; mean sign-recovery accuracy = 0.902; mean standardized RMSE = 0.305). The leakage-resistant repeated nested-CV model yielded AUC = 0.780 (95% CI 0.766–0.795); a matched complete-pipeline permutation test gave empirical p = 0.005. Stability-weighted SHAP and perturbation prioritized CKMT1B and KLK13 , whereas GNA13 , PANX2 , and all five sterol genes were not selected in any of 25 outer-fold models. The sterol genes retained modest score correlations but showed no model sensitivity. Across three lesion-progression cohorts, no pathway score remained associated with stage after FDR correction; in the cancer-only GSE151666 RNA-seq cohort, CombinedNet also showed no FIGO-stage trend. Conclusion This study supports directionality-aware transcriptomic scoring and a leakage-resistant feature-prioritization framework, but does not support GNA13 / PANX2 or cholesterol-biosynthesis signals as stable model drivers or the composite score as a validated lesion-stage biomarker. The findings remain hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

title: Профессор Стефания Яблонская – выдающийся дерматолог XX столетия
abstract: Стефания Яблонская, родившаяся в городе Могилеве, – всемирно известный ученый-медик и выдающийся профессор дерматологии. В ее необыкновенной биографии отразилась вся противоречивая история XX столетия. На протяжении 40 лет она занимала должность заведующей кафедрой дерматологии в Варшавском медицинском университете и руководила клиникой кожных и венерических болезней. В 1972 году Яблонская первой описала связь между вирусом папилломы человека и раком кожи при верруциформной эпидермодисплазии. За это открытие в 1985 году Яблонская и Орт были награждены медалью Роберта Коха. Профессор Яблонская является автором более чем 1000 публикаций, имеющих большое значение для изучения патогенеза и новых методов диагностики аутоиммунных буллезных заболеваний, заболеваний соединительной ткани и онкогенеза, индуцированного вирусом папилломы человека. В 1964 году Стефания Яблонская была избрана в научный комитет Международной лиги дерматологических обществ и была первым представителем Восточной Европы, а также первой женщиной, избранной в комитет. Stefania Jabłońska, born in Mogilev, is a world-renowned medical scientist and an outstanding professor of dermatology. Her extraordinary biography reflects the entire controversial history of the 20th century. For 40 years, she held the position of Head of the Department of Dermatology at the Warsaw Medical University and headed the Clinic of Skin and Sexually Transmitted Diseases. Thanks to her knowledge of languages (English, German, French, Russian), Professor Jabłońska was always aware of the achievements of world dermatology and introduced modern research methods and new therapies in her clinic. Being one of the most cited Polish doctors, she gained worldwide fame and was elected an honorary member of numerous foreign dermatological societies. In 1972, Stefania Jabłońska was the first to describe the link between human papillomavirus and skin cancer in verruciform epidermodysplasia. In collaboration with Professor Gerard Charles Jacques Orth, she characterized the molecular structure of the oncogenic virus, becoming the first to discover it in dermatological diseases. In 1985, Jabłońska and Orth were awarded the Robert Koch Medal for this discovery. Professor Stefania Jabłońska is the author of more than 1,000 publications that are of great importance for studying the pathogenesis and new diagnostic methods of autoimmune bullous diseases, connective tissue diseases and HPV-induced oncogenesis. In 1964, Stefania Jabłońska was elected to the scientific committee of the International League of Dermatological Societies and was the first representative of Eastern Europe, as well as the first woman elected to the committee.

title: Dynamic expression of ITGB1 in peripheral blood: a new biomarker for noninvasive diagnosis of squamous intraepithelial lesion to cervical cancer
abstract: Objective: Integrin β1 (ITGB1) plays a role in cancer progression; however, its potential as a blood-based biomarker in cervical carcinogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated the expression level of ITGB1 in the peripheral blood of patients with cervical cancer and precancerous lesions to evaluate its potential as a non-invasive biomarker. Methods: Multi-platform analyses, including bioinformatic screening (GEO/TCGA) and experimental validation, were conducted using clinical samples from the control, squamous intraepithelial lesion (SIL), and cervical cancer (CC) groups. The upregulation of ITGB1 expression across different sample types was thoroughly examined using several analytical methods. Results: The results showed that ITGB1 expression increased significantly with the progression of cervical disease in all sample types (all P < 0.05). High ITGB1 levels were associated with poor prognosis, with its expression predominantly localized to the membrane of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Significant differences in human papillomavirus (HPV) status and inflammatory markers (%NEUT, %LYMPH) were also observed among the groups. Conclusions: Overall, ITGB1 demonstrates potential as a reliable non-invasive biomarker for the early detection and monitoring of cervical cancer and its precancerous stages, showing consistent overexpression and strong clinical significance.

title: Structure-Based Evaluation of Theophylline as a Potential Inhibitor of HPV E6 and E7 Oncoproteins in Cervical Cancer
abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV-16 and HPV-18, serving as the primary etiological factor.The viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 promote cervical carcinogenesis through degradation of the tumour suppressors p53 and retinoblastoma protein (pRb), respectively, making them attractive therapeutic targets.In the present study, an integrated computational and experimental approach was employed to identify potential natural inhibitors targeting HPV E6 and E7 oncoproteins.A structure-based virtual screening of 120,823 phytobioactive compounds was performed using the Schrödinger Suite against homology-modelled E6 and E7 proteins.Lead compounds were further evaluated through molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT) analysis, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.Among the screened compounds, theophylline demonstrated the most favourable binding profile, exhibiting strong interactions with critical functional residues, including Cys58 in E6 and Arg65/Arg94 in E7, along with stable protein-ligand interactions throughout MD simulations.DFT analysis revealed favourable electronic properties, suggesting enhanced molecular reactivity and binding potential.In vitro investigations demonstrated significant antioxidant activity in the DPPH radical scavenging assay, with an IC50 value of 57.22 μg/mL, alongside notable anti-hemolytic and antiangiogenic properties.Collectively, these findings suggest that theophylline may interfere with HPV-mediated oncogenic pathways by destabilising E6/E7 functional interactions, restoring redox balance, and suppressing tumourpromoting mechanisms.The study highlights theophylline as a promising candidate for repurposing as a targeted therapeutic agent against HPV-associated cervical cancer, warranting further validation through cellular and in vivo studies.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Programming CRISPR Compartmentalization on DNA Origami for Multiplexed Biosensing
abstract: Abstract CRISPR-Cas12a has emerged as a transformative tool for nucleic acid detection and molecular diagnostics. However, achieving one-pot, orthogonal, multiplexed sensing remains challenging due to the nonspecific trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a. Here, we present a modular DNA origami-based platform that spatially confines and independently controls Cas12a activity, enabling simultaneous detection of multiple DNA targets within a single reaction. This spatial programming approach enables orthogonal one-pot detection of three DNA targets (EGFR L858R/Del19 mutations and HPV16) with minimal cross-talk, demonstrating 60% cleavage efficiency within 120 min at 100 nM. Through integrated molecular dynamics simulations and experimental validation, we identify an optimal ∼6 nm spatial window that maximizes cleavage efficiency, while the platform maintains robust performance in complex biological environments with a 10 nM detection limit in 20% serum. This compartmentalization strategy establishes a framework for spatially programming multi-enzyme systems on DNA nanostructures for synthetic biological circuits.

title: HPV vaccine uptake and barriers among adolescent girls and young women living in the urban slums of Kampala, Uganda
abstract: A high incidence of cervical cancer is evident in several low-income countries, particularly in the urban slums that harbor densely populated poor communities. Even though Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a key strategy for cervical cancer, the uptake remains low in these settings. This study assessed HPV vaccine uptake and barriers among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in the urban slums of Kampala, Uganda. We conducted a cross-sectional, concurrent mixed-methods study among 290 AGYW aged 15–24 years. Multistage sampling was used to recruit participants between August and October 2025. Quantitative data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with descriptive statistics and logistic regression in Stata 16.0. Qualitative data from focus group discussions were analyzed using thematic analysis. Of 290 AGYW (mean age 19.76 years, SD = 3.00), 30.7% reported receiving the HPV vaccine, and only 19.0% had completed the two-dose schedule. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination were lack of awareness, fear of side effects, and limited access to vaccination services. Proximity to a vaccination clinic (aOR 0.35; 95% Cl: 0.21–0.60) and healthcare worker counselling (aOR 0.19; 95% CI: 0.11–0.34) were each associated with significantly lower odds of remaining unvaccinated. Qualitative findings highlighted limited knowledge and misconceptions about HPV and the vaccine, parental influence on vaccination decisions, and health system barriers such as poor communication, inconsistent service availability, and negative healthcare experiences. Structural challenges, including distance to vaccination sites and transport limitations, further constrained access to HPV vaccination. HPV vaccine uptake among AGYW in Kampala’s urban slums remains low and was associated with low vaccine awareness, misconceptions, parental influence, and health system and structural barriers. Strengthening community sensitization, improving healthcare worker communication, and expanding community- and school-based delivery could improve equitable vaccine access and uptake, but further research is needed to assess the effectiveness of these strategies in this setting.

title: BRIDGING THE COVERAGE-PARTICIPATION GAP: BEHAVIORAL DETERMINANTS OF CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING AMONG WOMEN IN ADJARA, GEORGIA.
abstract: Cervical cancer (CCa) is largely preventable through human papillomavirus vaccination, organized screening, and timely management of precancerous lesions; however, screening participation may remain suboptimal even when services are formally available. This cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study examined behavioral and perceptual determinants of CCa screening participation among women in the Adjara region of Georgia. A total of 520 women aged 18-60 years from urban and rural municipalities were recruited using a convenience sampling approach; screening participation was interpreted primarily with reference to the nationally recommended screening age group of 25-60 years. Data were collected from October to December 2024 and analyzed between January and March 2025. The questionnaire was developed using a Health Belief Model-based framework supplemented by selected Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices components. The primary outcome was self-reported CCa screening participation, defined as having undergone screening at least once. Descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank correlation analysis, and multivariable logistic regression were used. Overall, 33.3% of participants reported previous cervical cancer screening. HPV vaccination coverage was 22.7%, while 43.8% of participants expressed willingness to receive vaccination. Perceived barriers were the most frequently reported Health Belief Model construct, followed by perceived benefits and positive attitudes toward screening. Screened women more frequently reported perceived benefits, positive attitudes, perceived susceptibility, cues to action, and healthcare provider recommendation than non-screened women. Spearman's rank correlation analysis showed that perceived benefits and self-efficacy were positively associated with screening participation, whereas perceived barriers were inversely associated with participation. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, perceived benefits were associated with increased odds of screening participation (aOR=1.80, 95% CI: 1.59-2.05, p<0.001), whereas perceived barriers were associated with reduced odds of participation (aOR=0.83, 95% CI: 0.77-0.89, p<0.001). Positive attitudes toward screening were also independently associated with screening uptake (aOR=1.24, 95% CI: 1.11-1.39, p<0.001). Knowledge score and perceived severity were not significant independent predictors. These findings indicate a persistent coverage-participation gap in Adjara and suggest that CCa screening uptake is associated mainly with behavioral, perceptual, and communication-related factors rather than knowledge or service availability alone. Thus, behaviorally informed, patient-centered, and provider-supported strategies are needed to reduce perceived barriers, strengthen perceived benefits and self-efficacy, and promote consistent healthcare provider recommendations. The low HPV vaccination rate and moderate willingness to be vaccinated further support the need for integrated CCa prevention strategies linking screening promotion with HPV vaccination communication.

title: HPV binding antibodies are associated with protection: a meta-analysis
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the major cause of cervical cancer globally. Current vaccines have shown high efficacy at preventing HPV infection and other surrogate disease endpoints in randomised controlled trials (RCT). However, uptake is limited by accessibility and cost. Rapid clinical evaluation is critical for shortening time-to-market and encouraging the development and deployment of affordable vaccines. We aim to establish a validated correlate of protection that will support vaccine developers and decision makers with vaccine development, approval, dose schedules and deployment decisions. Methods: We utilised three existing Cochrane Systematic Reviews of RCTs of HPV vaccines and extended these to 1st January 2026. We identified and extracted data from trials where both efficacy and immunogenicity (HPV-specific antibodies) were reported. For HPV types where vaccine efficacy was reported but not immunogenicity (Types 31/33/45/52/58) we sourced antibody binding concentrations from separate immunogenicity studies. We linked antibody binding concentrations from each RCT to the corresponding vaccine efficacy data, matching by study, vaccine arm, number of doses, and HPV type. We use a Bayesian framework in a model-based meta-analysis to examine the association between antibody binding concentrations and vaccine efficacy. Findings: Combining data on both vaccine-targeted and non-targeted HPV types, we find an association between type-specific antibody binding concentrations and vaccine efficacy against the three HPV outcomes tested: incident infection, persistent infection and grade 2 or 3 cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN2+) (p<0.0005, for all outcomes). We also compared this association with data from studies of natural infection, which had shown an association between antibody binding concentrations and risk of infection. This demonstrated that the association between vaccine-induced antibodies and vaccine efficacy was well aligned with the existing HPV literature on correlates of risk from natural exposure. Finally, we find evidence that the antibody concentrations associated with 50% (of the maximal) vaccine efficacy differ by type (p<0.0005, for example 16 sIU/ml for HPV58, but <0.5 IU/ml for HPV 16/18). Interpretations: HPV type-specific antibody binding concentrations are associated with protection against HPV related clinical outcomes, across different HPV types and vaccines, and after natural infection. The consistent observation that antibody binding concentrations correlate with protection provides support for the use of antibody binding for immunobridging, for example in non-inferiority studies when assessing similar vaccines. Funding: This work is supported by National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia and the University of New South Wales.

full_text: Abstract Cervical cancer, a significant global health challenge, is strongly associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV-16. The viral oncoproteins E5 and E6 are critical to HPV-mediated carcinogenesis, as they promote cell proliferation, immune evasion, apoptosis resistance, and genomic instability. E5 contributes to tumor progression by modulating growth factor signaling and promoting cell survival. E6, on the other hand, primarily drives malignant transformation by targeting the tumor suppressor p53 for degradation. Given their pivotal roles in cervical cancer, both oncoproteins are promising therapeutic targets. Recent advancements in gene-silencing technologies have provided novel opportunities for the selective inhibition of HPV oncogenes. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) and CRISPR/Cas-based genome-editing systems have demonstrated significant potential in suppressing E5 and E6 expression, restoring tumor suppressor functions, inducing apoptosis, and enhancing the sensitivity of cancer cells to conventional therapies. This narrative review summarizes the biological functions of HPV16-derived E5 and E6 in cervical carcinogenesis, and discusses recent developments in gene-silencing strategies targeting these oncogenes. Furthermore, it highlights current challenges, therapeutic limitations, and future perspectives for developing targeted molecular approaches aimed at cervical cancer prevention and treatment. E5 contributes to tumor progression by modulating growth factor signaling and promoting cell survival. E6, on the other hand, primarily drives malignant transformation by targeting the tumor suppressor p53 for degradation. Given their pivotal roles in cervical cancer, both oncoproteins are promising therapeutic targets. Recent advancements in gene-silencing technologies have provided novel opportunities for the selective inhibition of HPV oncogenes. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) and CRISPR/Cas-based genome-editing systems have demonstrated significant potential in suppressing E5 and E6 expression, restoring tumor suppressor functions, inducing apoptosis, and enhancing the sensitivity of cancer cells to conventional therapies. title_original: Targeting HPV16 E5 and E6 through gene-silencing approaches: mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and therapeutic perspectives

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the biological functions of HPV16-derived E5 and E6 in cervical carcinogenesis and explores gene-silencing strategies targeting these oncogenes for therapeutic applications. The central question is whether targeting E5 and E6 through gene-silencing approaches can effectively prevent or treat HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of preclinical studies on gene-silencing approaches targeting HPV16 E5 and E6. It does not report on systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. The evidence is derived from the biological mechanisms of E5 and E6, their roles in carcinogenesis, and the outcomes of gene-silencing interventions in experimental models.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that E5 and E6 are critical to HPV-mediated carcinogenesis, with E5 modulating growth factor signaling and promoting cell survival, while E6 primarily drives malignant transformation by degrading p53. Gene-silencing technologies, such as siRNAs and CRISPR/Cas-based systems, have shown significant potential in suppressing E5 and E6 expression, restoring tumor suppressor functions, and enhancing cancer cell sensitivity to conventional therapies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights challenges in translating preclinical findings to clinical applications, including the need for more research on the long-term safety and efficacy of gene-silencing strategies. It also notes the lack of data on the impact of these approaches in diverse populations and the need for further exploration of their mechanisms in vivo.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should prioritize the development of safe and effective gene-silencing therapies targeting HPV16 E5 and E6, with a focus on clinical trials and long-term safety assessments. It also emphasizes the importance of expanding studies to include diverse patient populations and exploring the potential of these strategies in combination with existing treatments.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the roles of HPV16-derived oncoproteins E5 and E6 in cervical carcinogenesis and evaluates gene-silencing approaches as potential therapeutic strategies. It highlights the critical functions of E5 in promoting cell survival and E6 in driving malignant transformation through p53 degradation. Preclinical evidence supports the use of siRNAs and CRISPR/Cas systems to suppress these oncogenes, restore tumor suppressor functions, and enhance cancer cell sensitivity to conventional therapies. However, the review identifies challenges in translating these findings to clinical practice, including safety concerns and the need for more research on diverse populations. Future research should focus on clinical trials, long-term safety, and combination therapies to advance targeted molecular approaches for cervical cancer prevention and treatment.
